data.title: User flows
body: # User flows
- **Notation:** oval — entry/exit · rectangle — command · diamond — branch · `[fs]` — filesystem work
Each flow is one user goal. The happy path first, then the error branches.
## Flow 1 — first run
**Goal:** get a working tracker in one command.
```mermaid
flowchart TD
A([npx kadence init]) --> B{Is this a git repository?}

B -- no --> B1[Error: kadence lives inside a repository
Hint: git init] --> Z([exit 1])
B -- yes --> C{Does .kadence/ already exist?}

C -- yes --> C1[We destroy nothing
Message: already initialised] --> Z2([exit 0])
C -- no --> D{Is git config user.email set?}

D -- no --> D1[Error with the exact command
git config user.email you@example.com] --> Z

D -- yes --> E[Create .kadence/events/
Append state.json to .gitignore
Create .kadence/README.md for the agent]
E --> F{Does AGENTS.md exist?}

F -- yes --> F1[Append a kadence section
leave what a human wrote alone]
F -- no --> F2[Skip]
F1 --> G[Show the 3 next steps]

**A decision worth noting.** `init` **does not create a commit**. The files appear in the working copy; the human commits. This comes straight from the boundary "never commit on the user's behalf" in [SPEC.md](../../SPEC.md).
## Flow 2 — the life of a task
**Goal:** carry a task from idea to `done`.
```mermaid
flowchart LR

A([kadence task add]) --> B[Write task.created
ULID + KAD-N]
B --> C([kadence task list])
C --> D{Is the task mine?}
D -- yes --> E([kadence task move KAD-42 in_progress])
E --> F[Write task.moved]
F --> G([work in the code])
G --> H([kadence task move KAD-42 done])
H --> I{Is the task in an open sprint?}
I -- yes --> J[Count it into velocity]
I -- no --> K[Just change the state]
**Every command that changes state appends exactly one event** — that is acceptance criterion M6.
## Flow 3 — working with an agent
**Goal:** the agent takes a task and works without a human retelling the context.
```mermaid
flowchart TD

A([The agent starts in the repository]) --> B[Reads .kadence/README.md
as an ordinary file]
B --> C([kadence task list --json])
C --> D{Is there a task in progress?}
D -- yes --> E([kadence task show KAD-42 --json])

D -- no --> F([kadence context --json
state for the current branch])
E --> G[The agent does the work]
F --> G
G --> H([kadence task move ... --json])

H --> I[An event with source: agent
from KADENCE_SOURCE=agent]
**The key difference from the competitors:** step B is reading a file, not a request to an MCP server. No network, no token and no running process are needed.
**Under `--json` there is only JSON on stdout.** Warnings go to stderr, otherwise the agent gets spoiled output — acceptance criterion M7.
## Flow 4 — merging branches
**Goal:** merge two people's work without sorting tasks out by hand. This is the flow where the product proves its claim.
```mermaid
flowchart TD
A([git merge feature-branch]) --> B{Conflicts in the event files?}

B -- no, and always so --> C[Git merges the journals
events are separate files]
C --> D([any kadence command])

D --> E{Does state.json match
the latest ULID?}
E -- no --> F[Rebuild the state from the journal]
E -- yes --> G[Take it from the cache]

F --> H{Were there concurrent events
about the same task?}
G --> H

H -- yes --> I[Show: N changes merged
KAD-42 from two branches, no conflicts]
H -- no --> J[The usual output]

**Step I is the same change from [prioritisation](DOC-30) that landed in v0.1.** Without it the product's main property works invisibly: the user never learns they have just avoided manual work, and so does not value it.
It has to be phrased as a fact, not a boast: "KAD-42: 3 changes merged from 2 branches" — and nothing more.
## Flow 5 — closing a sprint
**Goal:** get velocity out of real events. This is the main message of [positioning](DOC-29).
```mermaid
flowchart TD
A([kadence sprint close]) --> B{Is there an active sprint?}
B -- no --> B1[Error: there is no active sprint] --> Z([exit 1])
B -- yes --> C[Fold the journal over the sprint period]
C --> D{Are there tasks without an estimate?}

D -- yes --> D1[Warn: N tasks without an estimate
do not enter velocity]
D -- no --> E[Compute velocity]

E --> F[Compare the estimate with the fact
the time between in_progress and done]
F --> G[Write sprint.closed]

G --> H[Show the report:
velocity, divergence, carried-over tasks]
H --> Z2([exit 0])

**The warning about tasks without an estimate is not cosmetic.** The estimate is set in `task add`; if it was skipped, velocity will be understated and the person will not understand why. Better to say so plainly.
## Rules that cut across every flow
| Rule | Why |
| Outside a git repository — a clear error, never a stack trace | The first impression decides whether there is a second attempt |
| A command before `init` — an offer to run `init` | The most common beginner's mistake |
| Exit codes: `0` success, `1` execution error, `2` error in the arguments | Scripts and CI have to tell them apart |
| No command commits or pushes | A boundary from [SPEC.md](../../SPEC.md) |
| No command goes to the network | Offline is a property of the product |
## What of this becomes edge cases
Every diamond on the diagrams is a point where something can go wrong. The full analysis of them is in [edge-cases.md](DOC-19).
